A1.justification: Both PDFs describe GRAPES, with matching core methods and experiments. The complete main texts and appendices are readable, and figures, tables, and equations support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original node-classification experiments on twelve datasets, including memory measurements, sample-size tests, and sampling-entropy analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and adds PASS comparisons, estimator experiments, and analyses of hyperparameter sensitivity and sampled labels.

M1.justification: The principal GRAPES-RL/GFN procedures, Algorithm 1, and sampling losses remain unchanged. Appendix G adds experimental STE and STEN training variants that use perturbed top-k log-probabilities as classifier weights, with mean-one normalization in STEN.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same twelve node-classification datasets and retain their homophilous, heterophilous, multi-class, and multi-label coverage. New empirical analyses use existing datasets; the constructed graphs in Appendix H serve a theoretical proof.

E2.justification: v3 adds PASS to the main comparisons in Tables 1–2, AS-GCN to the memory comparison in Figure 3, and STE/STEN alternatives to the comparison in Table 6. These broaden comparisons with adaptive sampling and alternative gradient estimators.

E3.justification: Existing architectures, splits, training budgets, and sample-size sweeps are retained. The added PASS evaluation introduces full-batch inference and sampling_scope settings: normally 512, reduced to 128, 128, and 256 for Flickr, ogbn-arxiv, and ogbn-proteins, respectively.

E4.justification: v3 adds hyperparameter sensitivity analysis on Yelp (Appendix B.1), analysis of sampled label distributions across training (Appendix D), and comparisons of gradient-estimator variants on four datasets (Appendix G). Existing sample-size and entropy analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Appendix B.1 newly reports statistical estimates of hyperparameter importance and correlation with validation accuracy. Existing uncertainty conventions remain: ten-run means and standard deviations in Tables 1–2, five-run 95% confidence intervals for sample-size experiments, and node-wise entropy standard deviations. No increase in repeated-run counts is stated.

E6.justification: Under the same reported settings, snap-patents F1 changes from 26.26 ± 0.50 to 29.16 ± 0.54 for GRAPES-RL and from 28.46 ± 0.69 to 29.58 ± 0.24 for GRAPES-GFN. Other original main-table scores are retained. Substantial new results include PASS scores and four out-of-memory outcomes, AS-GCN memory measurements, STE/STEN scores, and Yelp sensitivity and label-distribution findings.

T1.justification: v3 introduces featureless/feature-based sampling definitions, a theorem claiming an adaptive-versus-non-adaptive accuracy separation, and Appendix H's proof, expected-homophily derivation, and GCN construction. Section 4 also adds complexity statements. The existing GFlowNet derivations remain.

C1.justification: The introduction adds a theoretical separation claim for a particular graph family. Performance contributions are stated more specifically for multi-label classification on heterophilous graphs, and the memory claim strengthens from 'up to an order of magnitude' in v2 to 'orders of magnitude' in v3's abstract and contribution list.

C2.justification: v3 adds interpretations connecting Yelp sampling to fewer labels per node, sensitivity chiefly to the classifier learning rate, and estimator or memory behavior to computational design. Section 7 explicitly limits observed gains to some heterophilous graphs and calls for identifying favorable graph characteristics. The earlier explicit limitation about evaluating only one fixed-depth GCN is omitted.

D1.justification: v3 documents PASS inference and sampling_scope adjustments, STE/STEN implementation details, and a PyTorch-versus-TensorFlow qualification for memory comparisons. Appendix B.1 changes the hyperparameter repository pointer from GitHub to an anonymous repository, while the abstract retains GitHub. Existing hardware, epoch schedules, and tuning ranges remain.

R1.justification: Related work expands to discuss MVS-GNN, FairSample, DSpar, and graph lottery-ticket methods. Supporting citations are added for STE, universal approximation, experiment tracking, and a GNN acceleration survey; the DAS6 infrastructure citation is removed. The established positioning around task-adaptive sampling remains.

P1.justification: Most existing method and experimental prose is retained. Local revisions affect the abstract, introduction, contribution list, and conclusion; limitations move into a separate section. Citation style, author affiliations, and acknowledgements also change.

P2.justification: v3 changes typography, margins, author layout, and table formatting throughout. It adds Figures 2, 8, and 9 and Tables 3 and 6, adds PASS and ranking rows to the main tables, and extends the memory plot with AS-GCN. Existing sample-size and entropy plots are retained and renumbered.

improvement.justification: The added PASS/STE comparisons and Yelp diagnostics strengthen empirical scrutiny. However, the new theoretical contribution contains a clear proof error: Appendix H.1 asserts a probability bound that, for L = K = 1 and N = 8, requires 1/7 <= 1/8. The empirical gains coexist with an unsupported new central theoretical claim, preventing a reliable net quality judgment.
